headline: FDA endorsed phase two STEM smart trial design for treatment-resistant Crohn's disease; Australian arm to open by end of 2025, US arm mid-2027; targeting 30% of a $13B market that fails biologic drugs
reasoning: NeuroScientific has received pre-IND meeting endorsement from the FDA for its stem cell-based therapy targeting refractory Crohn's disease patients who have failed biologic drugs. The FDA approved the trial design, reinforced the safety profile and historical human safety data to the point of nullifying animal pre-clinical testing requirements. The only condition was adding an adventitious virus assay to the manufacturing process, which the company agreed to and is implementing without delay. The Australian arm of the phase two trial is planned to open by end of 2025, with patient treatment starting early next year and US clinical sites opening mid-2027. The company is funded through trial initiation, with further funding plans being developed. The addressable market is characterised as 30% of a $13 billion Crohn's disease market with an unmet medical need not served by existing biologics like Stelara or Humira.
quote: So right now the big biologic drugs like Stelara or Humira are really what how Crohn's disease is being treated, right? So when you have severe Crohn's, you take, you know, you go through steroids and then you get into biologic drugs. And those are really the big hitters when it comes to Crohn's disease. The big problem is that, you know, 30% of patients don't respond to the biologic drugs. So you've got a significant portion of this population that, you know, is taking biologic drugs with absolutely no relief. And eventually it gets so bad that they actually have to have surgery to remove their, you know, portions of their: because the Crohn's disease has, has the inflammation has caused scarring. So that's where we feel we can provide an option where for these patients that really have that doesn't, there's an unmet medical need there. And, and that we're talking about 30% of a $13 billion market here. So it's not a small market, it's a market that, that has a need for a new treatment option.
episode_title: Neuroscientific moves closer to clinical trial in fight against Crohn's disease
